source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.author: Francesco Orabona

scope: Theorem 15.30 second claim (constant step, proof left as exercise)
Printed proof and explicitly identified source dependencies
definition_kind: literal algorithm relation on source-admissible attained trajectories; no total off-domain algorithm invented

notation.D_squared: D^2 := max_{0 <= s <= T-1} B_psi(u;x_s); a proof-local notation, not a global diameter assumption
notation.indices: x_0 initialization; x_1,...,x_T decisions; the comparator u is fixed and universally quantified in V

assumptions.text: Finite-dimensional Euclidean ambient R^d; X is the domain of psi. Strict convexity invokes the convex-domain convention of Definition 6.3.
V is nonempty, closed and convex, V subset X. Algorithm prints V ⊂ X ⊆ R^d; theorem prints V ⊆ X. No boundedness or full-dimensionality premise.
psi:X -> R strictly convex and differentiable on int X; Theorem 15.30 additionally says closed. The algorithm does not itself list closedness of psi.
x_0 in int X. Source does not require x_0 in V.

ell_t:R^d -> (-infinity,+infinity], V subset dom ell_t; Theorem 15.30 requires ell_t subdifferentiable on V. Do not replace this with loss differentiability, global convexity, bounded gradients, or closed losses.
eta_1,...,eta_T > 0. Theorem literally adds eta_{t+1} <= eta_t for t=1,...,T; its proof only uses this for t=1,...,T-1.
Theorem requires x_t in int X for t=1,...,T, in addition to the algorithm initial x_0 in int X. Comparator u need only lie in V subset X, including boundary points.
For t=1,...,T choose x_t in argmin_{x in V} [ell_t(x)+(1/eta_t)B_psi(x;x_{t-1})]. Membership entails x_t in V and global minimization over V.
For the second claim eta_t=eta for all t=1,...,T, with eta>0 inherited. It is printed as Moreover under the same theorem.

order: choose x_t using current ell_t and prior state x_{t-1}
feedback.model: prescient function-level feedback; not ordinary predict-then-observe online feedback or a gradients-only oracle
feedback.probability: deterministic pathwise inequality; no filtration, probabilistic event, confidence parameter or independence assumption printed
feedback.adaptivity: No stochastic/adversarial nonanticipativity restriction added. The loss is available before the current decision.

claims.formula: forall u in V: R_T(u) <= (max_{0 <= s <= T-1} B_psi(u;x_s))/eta_T - sum_{t=1}^T B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1})/eta_t
claims.negative_terms: Every movement term is retained with its own eta_t. The terminal comparator term appears in the exact telescoping equality but is dropped for the displayed theorem.
claims.proof_status: Printed proof, with unresolved citation bridge G-optimality.

claims.formula: forall u in V: R_T(u) <= B_psi(u;x_0)/eta - (1/eta) sum_{t=1}^T B_psi(x_t;x_{t-1})
claims.negative_terms: Retains the entire movement sum. It does not replace the initial divergence by the previous-state maximum.
claims.proof_status: Explicitly left as an exercise at PDF278 printed p266. A plausible telescope route is recorded only as an unprinted exercise obligation.

horizon_conventions.positive: Printed variable-step formula requires T>=1 to define eta_T and a nonempty max over 0,...,T-1. This is implicit expression well-formedness, not an explicit printed T>=1 binder. T=1 has empty correction sum.
horizon_conventions.zero: Algorithm loop can be interpreted as empty when T=0, but the theorem gives no zero-horizon convention. The variable-step expression then has an undefined eta_0 and empty maximum. A constant-step extension would need an explicit convention and is not a printed claim.
horizon_conventions.off_by_one: Literal eta_{T+1} <= eta_T is requested by the theorem t=1,...,T phrase while the algorithm only supplies eta_1,...,eta_T. Do not silently normalize this source discrepancy.

well_definedness.attainment: The update is an argmin selection. Nonempty closed V and strictly convex closed psi alone do not constitute a printed proof that each composite objective attains its infimum. No total selector, fallback point, or existence theorem is given here.
well_definedness.uniqueness: The source uses membership in argmin; it supplies no separate existence/uniqueness theorem in this section. Do not assert an audited unique-total map.
well_definedness.interiority: Interiority of every chosen iterate is a theorem assumption, not a consequence proved from the algorithm. x_0 need not be feasible.
well_definedness.extended_values: All evaluated losses are finite because x_t,u lie in V subset dom ell_t. B is finite on X x int X. The definition of closed functions appears in Definition 2.16; extending psi outside X by +infinity is a possible convention, not explicitly implemented here.
